findings.title: Retry cleanup deletes workflow reminders for all methods
findings.body: The second OR branch only checks retryCount > 1 and does not also require method: WorkflowMethods.SMS (or scheduled: false). Because Prisma OR branches are independent, this SMS cron job can delete EMAIL and WHATSAPP WorkflowReminder rows whose retryCount ever exceeds 1, even if they are future/unsent reminders owned by other delivery flows. The retry deletion should be scoped to the same SMS reminders this handler manages.

findings.title: Missing message or recipient never increments retryCount
findings.body: Retry counting only happens when twilio.scheduleSMS returns falsy inside the `if (message?.length && sendTo)` block, or when an exception is thrown. If sendTo is missing/empty (for example booking.smsReminderNumber is null) or the rendered message is empty, the handler silently skips the reminder without incrementing retryCount or deleting/scheduling it. Such reminders are fetched again on every cron run until their scheduledDate passes, so this common invalid-recipient failure mode is not bounded by the new retry limit.

findings.title: Retry update inside catch can abort the whole cron run
findings.body: The catch block now performs an awaited prisma.workflowReminder.update without its own error handling. If that update fails, for example because the reminder was deleted between findMany and processing (booking cancellation/reschedule cleanup) or because of a transient DB error (P2025/connection error), the exception escapes the per-reminder try/catch, stops processing all remaining unscheduled reminders, and prevents the success response. Previously the catch only logged and continued to the next reminder.

findings.title: Retry increment uses stale read-modify-write value
findings.body: Both retry paths write `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` using the value fetched at the start of the run instead of an atomic `{ increment: 1 }`. If two cron invocations overlap (or the row is updated concurrently), both can write the same next value, losing a failure count and allowing reminders to be retried more than twice or never reach the `retryCount > 1` deletion threshold.
